disagreements: Depth is detrend-method dependent at the ~10% level: my unmasked running-median detrend gives 494 / 566 / 640 ppm for 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 d windows, and a transit-masked re-detrend gives 606 / 614 / 657 ppm. The pipeline's quoted 638 ppm (pass 2, masked) sits at the upper end of that range; my preferred masked 1.0-d value is 614 +/- 72 ppm (-0.23 sigma from 638 +/- 78). My unmasked 1.0-d value (565 +/- 75) reproduces the pipeline's pass-1 565.4 ppm to 0.2 ppm. Any public number should carry a ~+/-60 ppm method systematic on top of the +/-72 ppm statistical error.
Duration: 2.33 h (fine BLS) / 2.25 h (box dchi2 scan) vs the pipeline's 2.44 h; a 0.1 h difference, within the grid resolution of both.

Period precision: an epoch-bootstrap gives P = 6.70362 +/- 0.00023 d; the pipeline's 6.703464 (stage 2), 6.703557 (screen) and 6.703512 (TLS) are all within 0.7 sigma, so quoting P to six decimals overstates the precision. t0 differs by 12.7 min (my 265.17436 vs 265.18316 BKJD), ~9% of the transit duration, consistent given the period-t0 covariance.

Shared caveat rather than a disagreement: the signal is ~2 sigma weaker in the last third of the data (my per-year depths 620 / 834 / 423 / 376 ppm, chi2 5.4 for 3 dof, max pairwise 2.05 sigma; the pipeline's quartiles 530 / 780 / 643 / 310 show the same pattern). Neither analysis flags it as significant, but it should be stated.

vet.json contains no SAP_FLUX depth; the SAP measurement and the two neighbour light-curve checks here are new information, not a comparison. Per-event scatter about a constant depth is chi2 182 / 124 dof in my events (pipeline 187 / 124): ~20% excess over the formal per-event errors, i.e. the per-event errors in events.csv are underestimated, although the random-phase box error already absorbs this at the folded level.
sap_vs_psf_depth: SAP_FLUX box depth at the same ephemeris (same 1.0-d running-median detrend): 265 +/- 32 ppm unmasked (301 +/- 31 masked) vs PSF 565 +/- 75 (614 +/- 72). Ratio SAP/PSF = 0.47 +/- 0.08 (0.49 masked). The stitched SAP aperture carries ~2.07x the PSF flux (raw per-quarter FLUX/SAP = 0.46-0.65, mostly ~0.47), so the expected ratio if the eclipse is on the PSF-modelled target is 0.48; the measured ratio matches it in every quarter (per-quarter ratios 0.37-0.58 vs expected 0.46-0.65). Equivalently the absolute deficit is the same in both products: 1.07 +/- 0.14 e/s (PSF) vs 1.04 +/- 0.12 e/s (SAP), ratio 0.97 +/- 0.17. The header CROWDSAP (0.72-0.85) would instead predict a ratio of ~0.77, 3.7 sigma from the measurement; CROWDSAP and the PSF flux are mutually inconsistent in this product (they imply target fluxes of ~3010 vs ~1890 e/s), so I treat the raw-flux expectation as the usable one. Implication: the eclipsing source's flux is captured to the same absolute extent by the PSF fit and by the aperture, which is what the target (or a source blended with it inside ~1 px) would give; a resolved neighbour whose variability only leaks partially into the PSF fit would give a larger SAP deficit than PSF deficit. Direct neighbour tests (new downloads, scratchpad only): the TPF host KIC 9655236 (G=16.4, 9.35 arcsec) shows -33 +/- 32 ppm PSF / -21 +/- 25 ppm SAP at the ephemeris, i.e. -0.13 +/- 0.12 e/s: excluded as the origin. The G=15.9 star KIC 9655226 at 5.23 arcsec (3.2x the target's flux; only Q3 and Q10 overlap the target's quarters) shows +56 +/- 39 ppm PSF = 0.34 +/- 0.24 e/s, 2.6 sigma below the target's 1.07 +/- 0.14 e/s deficit, and +95 +/- 29 ppm SAP = 0.62 +/- 0.19 e/s, consistent with its 4-pixel aperture (1.3 px from the target) catching part of the target's dip. If the signal originated on KIC 9655226 its own PSF deficit should be at least as large as the target's; it is not. Its narrow-window BLS has a weak peak at 6.70455 d (dlogL 14.3 vs window mean 5.9 +/- 1.8, depth 188 ppm) but at a phase 31 h away from the target's transits and no excess at the target's exact period (dlogL 7.9), so it is not the same events. Net: the dilution evidence favours the target (or an unresolved blend with it) over both catalogued bright neighbours, with the caveat that the pipeline's own pixel localisation is weak (median peak SNR 3.1, deficit a median 4.6 arcsec from the target and closer to the target than to any other Gaia source in only 2 of 6 usable quarters).

# kic-009655224 independent re-derivation (run id `poolA_main/adversarial/kic-009655224/rederive`, 2026-10-17)

Candidate language throughout: this is a *signal* in a KBONUS-BKG background-dwarf light curve, not a planet. All numbers below trace to `rederive_results.json`, `rederive_supplement.json`, `rederive_supplement2.json` and the two `neighbour_check_*.json` files in the run directory; the pipeline's `vet.json`/`pixel.json` were opened only after `run.log`, `supplement.log` and `supplement2.log` were written (timestamps in the directory listing). No code under `pipeline/` was read or imported; no wotan, lightkurve or TLS.

## 1. Data and method (own code: `rederive_kic009655224.py`)
- Cached FITS, extension `LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED`, `SAP_QUALITY == 0`, finite and positive FLUX and SAP_FLUX: 39,004 cadences over 1210.9 d, quarters 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15 (the star is on the failed-module channels for Q7/Q11/Q13 and has no Q0-2/Q16-17 PSF photometry). Kp 17.1, G dwarf (Teff 5170 K, Rstar 0.83, 2.2 kpc) from the pool table.
- Per-quarter median normalisation (the stitched FLUX and SAP_FLUX are already rescaled per quarter to common levels: raw per-quarter FLUX medians run 1470-2633 e/s, SAP 2677-5718 e/s; `rederive_supplement.json: raw_per_quarter`).
- Detrend: iterated time-windowed running median, 1.0 d window, trend points masked at >3 sigma up / >8 sigma down, final clip 4/8 sigma; 38,861 cadences survive. Point-to-point MAD scatter 1689 ppm (PSF), 807 ppm (SAP).

## 2. Blind BLS 1-50 d (astropy BoxLeastSquares, own grid)
- Grid: dP = dur_min P^2 / (3 T) with dur_min = 0.04 d, 89,004 periods; durations 0.04-0.30 d (8 values); objective = likelihood; per-quarter MAD as dy.
- **Top peak: P = 6.70377 d**, which is the pipeline's period (fractional offset 4e-5). Top-3 on the median-detrended spectrum: 6.70377 d (dlogL 27.3), 1.43429 d (14.9), 3.35218 d (14.4 = P/2 alias); on the raw spectrum 6.70377, 1.43429, 13.40816 d (2P alias).
- **BLS SDE 15.6** (median-detrended power; 14.2 raw) on the full PSF-flux data set. **Inverted-flux null (2 - f), identical grid: SDE 7.1** (6.6 raw), top period 1.29 d. Real/inverted reported together as the repo rules require.
- `recovered_blind = true`.

## 3. Statistics at the best ephemeris (PSF flux, full data set)
- Fine BLS (+/-0.4%, 25 durations): **P = 6.703660 d, t0 = 265.17436 BKJD (BJD 2455098.17436), duration 2.33 h** (box dchi2 scan over 0.5-6 h: 2.25 h). Epoch-bootstrap (120 resamples of transit epochs): P = 6.70362 +/- 0.00023 d. First/second half of the data give 6.70385 / 6.70401 d; the second half is weaker (dlogL 12.4 vs 29.8; depth 414 +/- 111 vs 723 +/- 117 ppm at the global ephemeris).
- Box depth = median(out-of-transit) - mean(in-box), error = std of the same box at 1500 random phases:
  - unmasked 1.0-d detrend (the blind-stage flux): **565 +/- 75 ppm, empirical SNR 7.5**, N_in = 557 (formal error 77 ppm; random-phase mean -46 ppm).
  - transit-masked re-detrend, 1.0-d window (post-detection refinement, labelled as such; `rederive_supplement2.json: masked_redetrend`): **614 +/- 72 ppm, SNR 8.5**. The unmasked estimate is biased low by the ~10% of in-window points that are in transit (expected ~70 ppm for a median with a 1-d window), which is exactly the gap observed.
  - window dependence: unmasked 494 / 566 / 640 ppm and masked 606 / 614 / 657 ppm for 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 d windows; excluding 0.5 d after every gap: 584 +/- 75 ppm.
- **Odd/even**: 594 +/- 104 vs 538 +/- 96 ppm, **0.39 sigma** (masked: 623 vs 605, 0.14 sigma).
- **Secondary at phase 0.5**: **-37 +/- 73 ppm (-0.51 sigma)**; deepest box anywhere in phase 0.2-0.8 is 145 ppm at phase 0.39 (2 sigma, consistent with noise).
- **Per-year depths** (Kepler years by quarter group): Y1 (Q3-4) 620 +/- 184, Y2 (Q5-8) 834 +/- 158, Y3 (Q9-12) 423 +/- 140, Y4 (Q14-15) 376 +/- 158 ppm; chi2 = 5.4 for 3 dof, largest pairwise difference 2.05 sigma. Per-quarter chi2 9.5 / 9 dof.
- **Transits**: 125 epochs with in-box data (124 with >= half coverage, 115 fully covered) out of 180 cycles. Weighted per-event mean 558 +/- 67 ppm; per-event chi2 about a constant 182 / 124 dof; 72% of events negative-flux; the top 1 / top 3 events carry 6% / 15% of the summed (depth/err)^2 and the depth without the three strongest events is 503 +/- 74 ppm, so no single-event dominance.

## 4. SAP_FLUX and dilution
SAP depth 265 +/- 32 ppm (301 +/- 31 masked); SAP/PSF = 0.47 +/- 0.08. The raw FLUX/SAP flux ratio is ~0.47 in every quarter, so the ratio expected if the eclipse is on the PSF-modelled target is 0.48: matched. In absolute terms the deficit is 1.07 +/- 0.14 e/s in PSF and 1.04 +/- 0.12 e/s in SAP (ratio 0.97 +/- 0.17). The header CROWDSAP values (0.72-0.85) would predict 0.77 and are internally inconsistent with the PSF flux level in this product, so they are not used. Two bright neighbours were tested directly with the same code on freshly downloaded KBONUS files (kept in the scratchpad `untrusted_dl/` directory, not in the repo cache):
- KIC 9655236, the TPF host (G 16.4, 9.35"): -33 +/- 32 ppm PSF, -21 +/- 25 ppm SAP = -0.13 +/- 0.12 e/s. Not the source.
- KIC 9655226 (G 15.9, 5.23", 3.2x the target's flux; PSF photometry only in Q3, 7, 10, 11, 13, so only Q3 and Q10 overlap): +56 +/- 39 ppm PSF = 0.34 +/- 0.24 e/s, 2.6 sigma below the target's deficit; +95 +/- 29 ppm SAP = 0.62 +/- 0.19 e/s, consistent with partial capture of the target's dip by a 4-pixel aperture 1.3 px away. A weak narrow-window BLS peak in its PSF flux at 6.70455 d (dlogL 14.3 vs 5.9 +/- 1.8) is 31 h out of phase with the target's transits and absent at the target's exact period (dlogL 7.9), so it is not the same events; it is noted, not interpreted.
Reading: the dilution pattern favours the target (or something blended within ~1 px of it) over both catalogued bright neighbours. This does not replace pixel-level localisation; the pipeline's own `pixel.json` summary (median peak SNR 3.1; deficit a median 4.6" from the target; closer to the target than to any other Gaia source in only 2 of 6 usable quarters; Gaussian-at-target beats scaled-image in 5 of 6) is weak and remains the open question for this signal.

## 5. Comparison with the pipeline (`vet.json`, stage-2 rules v1.5, stage2_pass = true, known_matches = [])
| quantity | pipeline | this re-derivation | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| period | 6.703464 (stage 2) / 6.703557 (screen) / 6.703512 (TLS) | 6.70366 refined; 6.70362 +/- 0.00023 bootstrap | 0.7 sigma |
| t0 (BKJD) | 265.18316 | 265.17436 | 12.7 min |
| duration | 2.44 h | 2.33 h (2.25 h box scan) | 0.1 h |
| depth | pass 1 565.4; pass 2 638 +/- 78 | unmasked 565 +/- 75; masked 614 +/- 72 | 0.2 ppm; -0.23 sigma |
| SNR | 8.2 (pass 2); TLS SNR 7.5, TLS SDE 13.2 | 7.5 unmasked / 8.5 masked; BLS SDE 15.6 (inv. 7.1) | consistent |
| odd/even | 663 / 612 ppm, 0.33 sigma | 594 / 538 ppm, 0.39 sigma | consistent |
| secondary | -29 ppm, -0.37 sigma | -37 +/- 73 ppm, -0.51 sigma | consistent |
| n events | 125 (chi2 const 187/124) | 125 (182/124), per-event depths correlate at r = 0.86 over 109 matched epochs | consistent |
| time dependence | quartiles 530 / 780 / 643 / 310 | years 620 / 834 / 423 / 376 | same 2-sigma weakening late |
| SAP depth, neighbours | not in vet.json | 265 +/- 32 ppm, ratio 0.47; both bright neighbours negative | new |

`agrees_with_pipeline = true`. The honest disagreements are all at the method-systematic level: the depth depends on the detrend at the +/-60 ppm level (the quoted 638 ppm is the top of my range; 614 +/- 72 is my preferred number), the duration differs by 0.1 h, and the period should be quoted as 6.7036 +/- 0.0002 d rather than to six decimals.

## 6. What this does and does not establish
Established independently: a 6.7036-d, ~2.3-h, ~600-ppm box-shaped signal is the top blind BLS peak in the PSF flux with SDE 15.6 against an inverted-null SDE of 7.1; it is flat in odd/even, has no secondary, is spread over 125 events with no dominant event, and its SAP/PSF behaviour and the two neighbour light curves point at the target rather than the catalogued bright neighbours. Not established here: on-sky localisation (the pixel-level result is weak), the 2-sigma late-time weakening, and any physical interpretation; the implied radius (~2.2-2.3 R_earth for Rstar 0.83, from the pipeline) is only meaningful if the host is the target. This remains a signal awaiting pixel-level and red-team scrutiny, not a candidate.
